title: Mirror, Mirror
prompt: Return True if s reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case and anything that isn't a letter or digit.
hint: Filter with str.isalnum(), lowercase, then compare with its reverse [::-1].
cases: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

title: FizzBuzz, Obviously
prompt: Return a list of strings for 1..n: 'Fizz' for multiples of 3, 'Buzz' for 5, 'FizzBuzz' for both, else the number.
hint: Check the 'both' case first, or build the word up piece by piece.

title: Two Sum
prompt: Return [i, j] with i < j where nums[i] + nums[j] == target. There is exactly one answer.
hint: A dict from value -> index lets you find the partner in one pass.

title: Vowel Counter
prompt: Return how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u, any case) are in s.
hint: sum(1 for c in s.lower() if c in 'aeiou')

title: Backwards Talk
prompt: Reverse the order of words. Collapse runs of spaces to one and trim the ends.
hint: str.split() with no arguments already handles messy spaces.

title: Digital Root
prompt: Sum the digits of n, again and again, until one digit is left. Return it.
hint: Loop while n >= 10. (There's also a one-line math trick with % 9.)

title: Anagram Detector
prompt: Return True if a and b use the same letters the same number of times. Ignore spaces and case.
hint: sorted() or collections.Counter both work.

title: Squish It
prompt: Run-length encode s: 'aaabcc' becomes 'a3b1c2'.
hint: Walk the string and track the current char and its count. itertools.groupby is a shortcut.

title: Bracket Police
prompt: Return True if every (, [ and { in s is closed in the right order. Ignore other characters.
hint: Push openers on a stack; every closer must match the top.

title: The Missing Number
prompt: nums holds every number from 0 to n except one. Return the missing one.
hint: The sum of 0..n is n*(n+1)//2.

title: Turn It 90°
prompt: Return the square matrix rotated 90 degrees clockwise (as a list of lists).
hint: Reverse the rows, then transpose: zip(*rows).

title: Unbox Everything
prompt: Flatten a list that may contain lists, nested any number of levels deep.
hint: Recursion: if an item is a list, flatten it too.

title: Collatz Countdown
prompt: If n is even, halve it; if odd, do 3n + 1. Return how many steps it takes to reach 1.
hint: A while loop and a counter. collatz_steps(1) is 0.

title: When in Rome
prompt: Convert 1 <= n <= 3999 to a Roman numeral, e.g. 1994 -> 'MCMXCIV'.
hint: Use a table that includes the subtractive pairs: 900 'CM', 400 'CD', 90 'XC', ...

title: Secret Agent
prompt: Shift every letter k places along the alphabet, wrapping around. Keep case; leave other characters alone.
hint: ord() and chr() with % 26. Handle 'a' and 'A' bases separately.

title: Silver Medal
prompt: Return the second-largest distinct value in nums, or None if there isn't one.
hint: set() removes duplicates. Then sort, or track the top two.

title: Pascal's Triangle
prompt: Return row n of Pascal's triangle (row 0 is [1]).
hint: Each new row is 1, the sums of neighbours in the previous row, then 1.

title: Robot on a Grid
prompt: A robot starts top-left and can only move right or down. How many routes reach bottom-right?
hint: Each cell's count = cell above + cell to the left. (Or think combinations.)

title: Best Streak
prompt: Return the largest sum of any non-empty run of consecutive numbers in nums.
hint: Kadane: keep the best sum ending here = max(x, previous + x).

title: Snail Trail
prompt: Return all items of the matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting top-left.
hint: Take the first row, rotate what's left counter-clockwise, repeat.

title: Gossip Counter
prompt: Return the most common word (lowercase, letters only). Break ties alphabetically.
hint: re.findall(r'[a-z]+', text.lower()) then a Counter.

title: Prime Time
prompt: Return True if n is a prime number.
hint: Only check divisors up to the square root of n. Remember 0 and 1.
